stdout:
# Checkpoint

Issue: exported YAML/JSON import fails on nested metadata or a leading JSON `#` line.

Changes:
- YAML import decoder uses `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`, so nested mappings in metadata and attachments decode with string keys.
- JSON decoder skips one first line only when its first byte is `#`.
- Removed attachment map conversion; the decoded value now marshals directly to JSON.
- Added focused import tests for YAML, JSON, JSON with a header, namespace fields, nested metadata and attachments, and rejection of a second/later JSON comment line.

Checks:
- `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./internal/ext` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./cmd/flipt` — interrupted after extended silence (exit 130); CLI package result remains unverified. This was an additional check; the import package suite passed.

Local tooling: `rg` unavailable; used `find`/`grep` for searches. No downloads requested.

+package ext
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/rpc/flipt"
+	"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
+	"google.golang.org/grpc/status"
+)
+
+func TestImportNestedMetadata(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name     string
+		encoding Encoding
+		input    string
+	}{
+		{
+			name:     "YAML",
+			encoding: EncodingYAML,
+			input: `# export header
+version: "1.4"
+namespace:
+  key: projects
+  name: Projects
+  description: Project flags
+flags:
+  - key: active
+    name: Active
+    enabled: true
+    metadata:
+      owner: team
+      settings:
+        regions: [us, eu]
+        options:
+          live: true
+          count: 2
+    variants:
+      - key: first
+        attachment:
+          nested:
+            items: [{name: example}]
+`,
+		},
+		{
+			name:     "JSON",
+			encoding: EncodingJSON,
+			input:    `{"version":"1.4","namespace":{"key":"projects","name":"Projects","description":"Project flags"},"flags":[{"key":"active","name":"Active","enabled":true,"metadata":{"owner":"team","settings":{"regions":["us","eu"],"options":{"live":true,"count":2}}},"variants":[{"key":"first","attachment":{"nested":{"items":[{"name":"example"}]}}}]}]}`,
+		},
+		{
+			name:     "JSON with header",
+			encoding: EncodingJSON,
+			input:    "# export header\n" + `{"version":"1.4","namespace":{"key":"projects","name":"Projects","description":"Project flags"},"flags":[{"key":"active","name":"Active","enabled":true,"metadata":{"owner":"team","settings":{"regions":["us","eu"],"options":{"live":true,"count":2}}},"variants":[{"key":"first","attachment":{"nested":{"items":[{"name":"example"}]}}}]}]}`,
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, tc := range tests {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			creator := &mockCreator{getNSErr: status.Error(codes.NotFound, "missing")}
+			err := NewImporter(creator).Import(context.Background(), tc.encoding, strings.NewReader(tc.input), false)
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			require.Equal(t, []*flipt.CreateNamespaceRequest{{Key: "projects", Name: "Projects", Description: "Project flags"}}, creator.createNSReqs)
+			require.Len(t, creator.createflagReqs, 1)
+			require.Equal(t, "projects", creator.createflagReqs[0].NamespaceKey)
+			require.Equal(t, map[string]any{
+				"owner": "team",
+				"settings": map[string]any{
+					"regions": []any{"us", "eu"},
+					"options": map[string]any{"live": true, "count": float64(2)},
+				},
+			}, creator.createflagReqs[0].Metadata.AsMap())
+			require.Len(t, creator.variantReqs, 1)
+			require.Equal(t, "projects", creator.variantReqs[0].NamespaceKey)
+			var attachment any
+			require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(creator.variantReqs[0].Attachment), &attachment))
+			require.Equal(t, map[string]any{"nested": map[string]any{"items": []any{map[string]any{"name": "example"}}}}, attachment)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestImportJSONSkipsOnlyFirstHeaderLine(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, input := range []string{
+		"# first\n# second\n{}",
+		" \n# later\n{}",
+	} {
+		err := NewImporter(&mockCreator{}).Import(context.Background(), EncodingJSON, strings.NewReader(input), false)
+		require.Error(t, err)
+	}
+}
